posts.title: Why AI Agents Need Observable Runtime Receipts
posts.description: The modern web is increasingly difficult for legitimate machines to observe. Agents need explicit runtime receipts, not confident guesses.
posts.tokenSummary: Essay arguing that AI agents need observable runtime receipts because modern websites are shaped by bot protection, 429s, JavaScript-only rendering, hidden state, crawler ambiguity, and explicit diagnostics.

posts.title: The Agent-Readable Web
posts.description: Why websites may need small, honest runtime receipts for routes, crawl status, artifacts, and limits.
posts.tokenSummary: Essay arguing that websites need small, honest runtime receipts for routes, crawl status, warnings, artifacts, and limits so humans and agents can inspect systems without guessing.

posts.title: The Moment a Framework Becomes a Tool
posts.description: On the shift from an interesting framework repository to a tool that can generate runnable, inspectable systems.
posts.tokenSummary: Project note about Paideia crossing from framework repository to usable tool through the init command, emphasizing generated project polish, runtime trust, disciplined scope, and small understandable systems.

posts.title: Why Generated Systems Should Explain Themselves
posts.description: Why generated software should expose its shape, contracts, capabilities, and security-relevant runtime facts.
posts.tokenSummary: Developer-facing essay explaining why generated systems should expose runtime identity, artifact inventories, capabilities, diagnostics, and security-relevant facts.

posts.title: Building Paideia: Software That Explains Itself
posts.description: Why I am building Paideia as a small framework for readable, inspectable, self-describing software systems.
posts.tokenSummary: Long-form positioning essay about building Paideia as a small framework for self-describing generated systems with runtime identity, artifact inventory, deterministic build IDs, capabilities, diagnostics, and inspectability.
